risks: Combined compose destroys prior provider draft before new create is confirmed; save rejection can lose accessible draft and submission rejection loses newly created ID in errorResult.

Autosave files are repeatedly uploaded and reopened draft attachments are dropped; attachment-only edits are not dependencies of the autosave effect; pending save clears dirty even if user edited while awaiting it.

Caller-controlled blob/path metadata is not source-message ownership evidence; stat/readFile supplies per-file size/type but there is no aggregate/MIME/finalized immutable object boundary in current prepare.
Submission acceptance and recipient delivery differ. SMTP unknown effect and provider read-back capability limits cannot be fixed by unique DB receipts or blind retries.
Forward originals must be preserved as provenance without reusing source Message-ID as new outgoing ID or silently asserting forward threading semantics unsupported by provider.
Three shared normative new files collide with WP-17/WP-18; two migration identifiers may describe overlapping schema; root must allocate ownership and selected migrator names.

Domain SendDraft baseRevision:number/status accepted|pending|ambiguous differs from published operation draftRevision:string and Rox2 canonical status envelope; explicit mapping and schema error precedence are required.

Published full DoD includes common search, mentions, notifications, activity and agent/MCP seams absent from inspected package surface; predecessor or root integration receipts are needed, not N/A labels.

Origin equality guard must be preserved; fetch redirects and provider error descriptions require targeted credential/privacy verification rather than assuming current helper tests prove all URL boundaries.
Whole-file working-tree evidence can become stale during lead integration; preflight validation is static-only and cannot establish feature completion.
